text.p: Lloyd's of London insurance syndicate 780, operated by managing agent B F Caudle, on Thursday announced a profit of 23.6 percent of allocated capacity for 1994.
This equates to 17.5 percent after personal expenses compared with a pure year profit of 47.41 percent for the 1993 year, Caudle said in a statement.
"This latest result follows last year's excellent return and should maintain the Syndicate's position as one of the top performing non-marine syndicates in the Lloyd's market," it added.
Lloyd's of London insurance market and its component syndicates report results three years in arrears to allow for most claims to be settled.
Caudle, whose only syndicate is 780, said the 1995 and 1996 accounts were on course to produce further profits, projecting 15 and 16 percent respectively before personal expenses.
Syndicate 780's capacity -- the amount of premium income it can underwrite -- in 1997 is 55 million stg, compared with 51.5 million in 1996.
Corporate capital provided 20.3 million stg of 1997 capacity, up from 14 million last year.
Lloyds of London yesterday issued updated profit estimates for the 170 or so syndicates in the market for the 1994, 1995 and 1996 years of account.
